title: FiniteStructureUnitLift
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], complete for an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated and finite type. Write $X_n=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ and $j_n:X_n\to X$. Let $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ be the canonical transition immersion, specified by both pullback projection equations. Let $c_n:i_n^*j_{n+1}^*\cong j_n^*$ be the canonical composition comparison of tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $p_n:Y_n\to X_n$ be finite, with $g_n:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ giving cartesian transition squares and $j_{n+1}\circ p_{n+1}\circ g_n=j_n\circ p_n$. Let $G$ be a coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] on $X$ with support proper over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base], and suppose isomorphisms $\psi_n:j_n^*G\cong p_{n,*}\mathcal O_{Y_n}$ commute with $c_n$ and the canonical affine base-change maps followed by the structure-sheaf pullback maps [lem-weil-pbc-affine-pushforward-base-change]. Put a_n:G to (j_n p_n)_* O_Yn equal to the adjoint of psi_n [lem-weil-pbc-finite-structure-adjoint-transitions]. Suppose mu:G tensor G to G is an O_X-linear symmetric product, with a_n(mu(x tensor y))=a_n(x)a_n(y) on every open. There is a unique O_X-linear map eta:O_X to G satisfying mu(eta(1) tensor x)=x on each open, and a_n(eta(r))=(j_n p_n)^sharp(r) for each scalar section r. This states only the unit step, without constructing any ring sheaf or algebra maps.

source.place: Stacks Tag 09ZT, multiplication paragraph; expanded using 088E, 088F and 0CYS. Read https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09ZT on 2026-10-13.

proof.text: Apply the existence part to obtain eta satisfying the left-unit law and scalar formula.

If eta and eta-prime satisfy the left-unit law, mu(eta(1),eta-prime(1)) equals eta-prime(1) by the first unit law and eta(1) by symmetry and the second law. Hence the two units agree over every open. Module linearity gives eta(r)=r eta(1), so their section maps agree on all scalars. Sectionwise extensionality proves uniqueness.
